headline: Warsh put prices first and September flipped to a coin-flip hike; US strikes on Iran gapped Brent above $90 into month end.
stance: Vol was sold every session into the podium, and the podium delivered: the curve bear-flattened and September went from a hold to a coin-flip hike. A short-vol book now meets an oil gap and the last business day of August in the same tape.

news.head: Warsh: the Fed's focus 'right now should be on prices'
news.body: He called the 2% target firm and said he would be 'hard pressed to describe broad financial conditions as restrictive.' No September commitment.

news.head: September hike odds roughly doubled
news.body: Futures moved to about 60% on a 25bp increase from near 34% before the speech, with further increases priced across the following year.

news.head: US struck Iranian launchers at Larak Island
news.body: Brent $90.25 overnight, the first American action against Iran in over a month. Asia closed lower: Nikkei -1.1%, Kospi -1.5%.

news.head: China factory gauge still under 50
news.body: August manufacturing PMI improved to 49.8, still below the expansion line. Japan's industrial output and retail sales both beat forecasts.

implications: September is a two-sided meeting now, and the market has to carry that through a payroll print and a CPI before it gets an answer.
Gold sold through the strike headline and kept selling. When the metal ignores a Middle East escalation, the trade was rates positioning, not risk.

watch.head: Month end, last business day
watch.body: The turn settles into an empty reverse-repo facility with reserves at their lowest since April. Friday's funding marks are a stale read on today.

watch.head: ISM manufacturing and job openings, Tuesday 10am ET
watch.body: The first data he gets after ranking the mandate. Manufacturing was 55.6 last month; a second strong print makes September harder to argue against.

watch.head: Jobs report, Friday 8:30am ET
watch.body: July payrolls were negative at -23k with unemployment at 4.1%. The labour half of the mandate is the one argument left against a move.

watch.head: Fed decision, September 16
watch.body: Sixteen days out, with CPI on the 11th the last inflation read before it.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: Friday's repricing came out of the front end, not term premium. Warsh moved the September meeting; he did not touch the long-end supply story that ran all month.
It came out of real rates, with breakevens going the other way. The market graded him credible: tighter policy priced, not more inflation.
sections.positioning: Standing background, not new: the speculative long in the 2-year has been at a three-year maximum for a month, and Friday's move went straight through it.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: SKEW jumped Friday while front-end vol fell again. Desks bought the tail and sold the body into the podium: hedged for a gap, not de-risked for a trend.
Nasdaq vol closed the week under 20, one session before an oil gap and a hike repricing landed on it. The cheapest possible timing to have been short.
Breadth narrowed a second straight session while the index barely moved. S&P names above their 50-day fell to 53.4%. The average member is already selling.
sections.positioning: Spec net short VIX sits at the 7th percentile of three years and Nasdaq 100 futures at the 3rd. Nobody is paid to own downside into this open.

single_name.note: Matador Resources - insider buy filed Aug 28, above its 200-day, 6.3 days to cover. An E&P carrying real short interest into a Brent gap.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: Investment-grade spreads tightened every session last week and high yield's premium over them narrowed with it. Credit sat out the rates repricing entirely.
An oil gap is an input cost, not a default cycle. But at a high-yield premium this thin there is no room left to absorb a second one.
sections.positioning: Primary-dealer high-yield inventory sits at the 12th percentile of three years. Dealers carry almost nothing into a week that opens on an oil gap and closes on payrolls.

single_name.note: Chicago Atlantic Real Estate Finance - three insider rules fired and a filing Aug 28, above its 200-day. A lender bid by its own board.
